external_sources.title: Government careers guidance: writing a CV
external_sources.supports: A CV summarises relevant skills, learning and experience. Tailor it to the role, update it and check accuracy. This classroom draft omits private contact and referee details.

external_sources.title: Government careers guidance: application forms
external_sources.supports: Read the form and role requirements; match truthful experience to the questions; review the completed form. School or voluntary experience may be relevant. This is an offline practice form, not a submitted application.

evidence.description: A completed anonymous practice application responding to a fictional role brief, with a learner-owned example, accuracy/relevance review, revision, support record and visible unresolved gaps; no submission or selection outcome is claimed.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: answer one box at a time with help.
routes.Independent: Independent: complete and check the form.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: improve a response against the brief.

vocab.definition: A form asking to be considered for a role.
A specific event or action that shows a skill.
Something not yet known or complete.

cases.text: A form asks why this role interests you. The answer lists only a favourite meal.
cases.fact: No link to the role is explained.
cases.next_step: State an honest interest linked to a task or skill in the brief.
cases.staff_note: A learner may decide the role is not for them and give a reason.

cases.text: The form asks for teamwork. The learner describes their part in a real class task.
cases.fact: The response links their action to the skill.
cases.next_step: Explain what they did and any help used.
cases.staff_note: Paid experience is not the only relevant experience.

cases.text: A box asks for a course result that is not yet confirmed.
cases.fact: An achieved result is not known.
cases.next_step: Record in progress or to check, as accurate, then ask staff.
cases.staff_note: Do not invent a grade or award.

cases.text: The form says use short answers. A long response does not address the task.
cases.fact: Length has not made the answer relevant.
cases.next_step: Keep the key action and reason that answer the question.
cases.staff_note: Accept concise speech or scribing as an accessible response.

cases.text: The applicant cannot confirm whether a proposed time is possible.
cases.fact: A commitment has not been checked.
cases.next_step: Mark it to check with the appropriate adult before agreeing.
cases.staff_note: No availability is filled in for the learner.

cases.text: All boxes contain words, but one example was copied from the adult model.
cases.fact: A filled box is not proof the experience belongs to the learner.
cases.next_step: Replace it with a true example or an honest gap.
cases.staff_note: Check ownership before storing evidence; this form is not submitted.

CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W02 · Week beginning 9 November 2026
I Do: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Model each line aloud and make the reasoning explicit. Check the form answers the actual prompts: role/reference, interest, relevant skill and real example, learning/experience status, availability status, and a clear review. A to-check entry can be honest but does not prove the missing information is complete. Record the learner’s revision after feedback. Distinguish application-writing skill from a real job application; no consent, signature, reference, employment status or success outcome is prefilled.

We Do: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Read the hinge aloud, ask for a choice and a reason. B answers the question with authentic experience. A repeats requirements without evidence; C invents work history. A justified not-yet/to-check entry is better than a fabricated answer.

Purpose and success checks
How can I answer a job form clearly?
I can read what the form asks. I can match a true example to the role. I can check my form and name a gap.

CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W2-E1: A completed anonymous practice application responding to a fictional role brief, with a learner-owned example, accuracy/relevance review, revision, support record and visible unresolved gaps; no submission or selection outcome is claimed.
Before pupils arrive

Bring the Week 1 CV draft if it exists; if missing, record the gap and use an actual class-task example elicited now. Print the practice form and vacancy brief. Prepare usual literacy/communication supports. No real employer, account, application portal or submission is involved.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Where this leads
This helps me give clear, truthful answers when I apply for work or training.
Forty minute sequence
Slide
Min
Action
Open title and big question before timing.
Private check-in, quiet start and support choice.
Read the diagram; hear one clue or question.
Read the exact objective and success checks.
Model the six lines; explain the reason for each.
Ask for a hinge answer and reason; reteach if needed.
Use the six cards and the Supported/Independent/Aspire routes.

Hidden reference for adults.
Hinge and reteach

B answers the question with authentic experience. A repeats requirements without evidence; C invents work history. Ask which part the learner did and whether the example matches the question. Reteach with a clearly labelled adult example, then ask the learner to choose their own. A justified not-yet/to-check entry is better than a fabricated answer.
Access and practice
Supported: answer one box at a time with help. Independent: complete and check the form. Aspire: improve a response against the brief.

Read the vacancy and instructions; work through the form one box at a time. Use Week 1 material only where it is authentic and relevant. Offer reading or exact scribing, then record the help. Give one NS+ prompt to improve relevance or accuracy; keep the learner’s own response. Do not send the form.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Use learner ID only. Keep personal contact details, school and staff names, health/disability information and referee details out of the practice form. No signatures or commitments are required. Use truthful learner examples and mark unknowns. Staff check any real future application separately through the agreed private route.
Assessment and feedback

Check the form answers the actual prompts: role/reference, interest, relevant skill and real example, learning/experience status, availability status, and a clear review. A to-check entry can be honest but does not prove the missing information is complete. Record the learner’s revision after feedback. Distinguish application-writing skill from a real job application; no consent, signature, reference, employment status or success outcome is prefilled.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school’s evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio

Read or listen to an instruction, explain a relevant example, ask a clarifying question and respond to feedback. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Staff answers and response guide
Complete a practice application
These are possible responses and task guides, not learner observations. Accept a defensible answer based on the facts or actual work. Record each learner’s reasoning and support.
Card key
Card
Judgement or step
Possible action
A
Does not answer the question. No link to the role is explained.
State an honest interest linked to a task or skill in the brief.
B
Relevant evidence. The response links their action to the skill.
Explain what they did and any help used.
C
Needs checking. An achieved result is not known.
Record in progress or to check, as accurate, then ask staff.
D
Needs editing. Length has not made the answer relevant.
Keep the key action and reason that answer the question.
E
Availability unconfirmed. A commitment has not been checked.
Mark it to check with the appropriate adult before agreeing.
F
Not authentic evidence. A filled box is not proof the experience belongs to the learner.
Replace it with a true example or an honest gap.
Model and hinge

Adult example: Explain a time you checked work. Task: I had to sort class kit by label. Action: I checked each item against the list. Result: I found one item in the wrong place. This example fits the role’s checking task. It is a model; use your own true experience.

B answers the question with authentic experience. A repeats requirements without evidence; C invents work history. Ask which part the learner did and whether the example matches the question. Reteach with a clearly labelled adult example, then ask the learner to choose their own. A justified not-yet/to-check entry is better than a fabricated answer.
Individual evidence key

Check the form answers the actual prompts: role/reference, interest, relevant skill and real example, learning/experience status, availability status, and a clear review. A to-check entry can be honest but does not prove the missing information is complete. Record the learner’s revision after feedback. Distinguish application-writing skill from a real job application; no consent, signature, reference, employment status or success outcome is prefilled.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: A learner may decide the role is not for them and give a reason.
Card B: Paid experience is not the only relevant experience.
Card C: Do not invent a grade or award.
Card D: Accept concise speech or scribing as an accessible response.
Card E: No availability is filled in for the learner.
Card F: Check ownership before storing evidence; this form is not submitted.
Common misunderstandings

A filled box is not automatically a good answer. Copying a model does not make it a personal achievement. Match the question before adding detail. A draft with an honest gap is not a submitted application.
Teaching boundary

Use learner ID only. Keep personal contact details, school and staff names, health/disability information and referee details out of the practice form. No signatures or commitments are required. Use truthful learner examples and mark unknowns. Staff check any real future application separately through the agreed private route.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
Assessment boundary
CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W2-E1 contributes to the source assessment. No criterion, registration or award completion is invented. Sources: FACTS_LEDGER.md.
